title: Tonkotsu Ramen
subtitle: Japanese rich pork bone broth noodle soup
excerpt: The ramen from Fukuoka: a thick, milky-white broth made from pork trotters and knuckles boiled vigorously for many hours until the collagen and fat emulsify into an intensely rich, opaque soup, served over noodles with chashu pork and a soft egg.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tonkotsu ramen (ton = pork, kotsu = bone) originates from Fukuoka city in Kyushu, southern Japan, and is the style most widely known outside Japan. Unlike shoyu ramen (which has a clear broth), tonkotsu is made by boiling pork bones at a vigorous simmer for six or more hours until the collagen from the bones and the fat emulsify into the cooking liquid, turning it creamy-white and opaque. The long boil is what creates the texture; a gentle simmer makes a clear consommé, not tonkotsu. The flavour is pure umami depth with a distinctive, slightly funky quality from the marrow and cartilage. This home version uses pork trotters (pig's feet) and pork belly, which are more available than the traditional pork neck bones.

content.text: The vigorous boil for several hours is not a mistake: it is what creates the milky, emulsified texture of tonkotsu broth. A gentle simmer produces a clear pork stock, not tonkotsu. Blanch the bones first to remove blood and impurities. This is a two-day recipe at home: make the broth and chashu pork on day one, assemble and serve on day two.

content.text: Day 1: make the broth: blanch the pork shoulder in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse. Cover with 3 litres of fresh cold water. Add the garlic, ginger, and 2 spring onions. Bring to a full rolling boil and cook uncovered and vigorously for 4 to 5 hours, adding water to keep the bones covered. The broth will turn opaque and creamy. Strain and season.

Make the chashu: simmer the rolled pork belly in 400 ml water, soy sauces, sugar, and aromatics for 2 hours. Cool in the liquid (this becomes the tare). Refrigerate overnight. Slice the cold chashu into 1 cm rounds.

To serve: cook the noodles briefly. Heat the broth and season with 2 tablespoons of tare per bowl. Place noodles in deep bowls. Pour hot broth over. Top with 2 chashu slices, a halved marinated egg, sliced spring onion, and a drop of sesame oil.
